edition.alertText: IRGC claims two supertankers hit mines; 28 incidents in October — UKMTO overwhelmed

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis deepened in the war's eighth month. UKMTO reported 29 warnings covering 28 incidents in October to date — the highest sustained attack pace since the war began on February 28. At least 16 confirmed attacks were logged in the week ending October 18. The Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride sank on October 14 after an IRGC projectile strike, bringing confirmed commercial sinkings to five since March. Kpler measured crude flows at 11.6 million barrels per day for the week to October 13, about 68% of the 17.1 million bpd pre-war baseline, though daily flows are wildly volatile — 20.8 million barrels transited on October 8 but only 2.9 million on October 11.

Iran's IRGC claimed on October 18 that two laden supertankers — each carrying over 2 million barrels of crude — hit naval mines and caught fire on unauthorized routes. JMIC says the claims are unsubstantiated. Oil prices rallied sharply last week: Brent settled at $109.86 on Friday (its first touch of $110 since May) before easing to $108.81 on Monday. WTI hit $101.41 Friday and slipped to $101.00. VLCC tanker rates remain near $1.3 million a day — 43 times the January level — with freight now making up 27% of delivered crude cost versus 3% pre-war.

Diplomatic efforts remain stalled. Iran's seven conditions for reopening the strait (set October 4) are still on the table. Trump has ruled out nuclear weapons and ground troops, saying the war will end after the November 3 midterm elections. The UN warns of a food security emergency as fertilizer shipments through the strait remain near zero and QatarEnergy has extended LNG cancellations into November. UKMTO says it is struggling to accurately report true attack numbers because many ships will not report being hit.

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 45% from pre-war. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Sulfur prices at record highs. MEG supplied ~35% of global urea and 25% of ammonia.

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz remain near zero. UN warns of food emergency as planting season approaches. Mosaic cut US phosphate output ~2M tonnes. OCP's last MEG sulfur cargo: April 10.

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: Qatar LNG (~20% of global trade) largely blocked. QatarEnergy extended cancellations into November. Europe 12-14% LNG was Qatar. Asian buyers switching back to coal — Newcastle at 3-year high ~$150/t.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint.
